title: Rust Native permission authority

trigger.user_goal: Make the Native permission system a coherent Rust authority without replacing Bubblewrap merely for implementation-language purity.
trigger.current_fact: Command policy and Native execution are already Rust, but permission kinds are stringly typed, request_permissions cannot produce a verified safe/trusted grant, mode behavior is partly encoded as bypass control flow, and the full eight-kind permission surface lacks one typed authority model.

security_invariants: Explicit grants bind OAuth owner, workspace, tool, permission kind, canonical argument digest, scope and expiry.
Once grants are atomically consumed at most once and concurrent replay cannot authorize two executions.
Session grants are process-local and disappear on restart.
Cross-owner, cross-workspace, cross-tool, argument-mutated, expired and revoked grants fail closed.
Network/destructive/environment grants widen only their named policy dimension.
Private vault absence, dropped Linux capabilities and workflow/project/finalizer non-inheritance remain invariant in every Native mode.

delivery.name: in-memory grant ledger with once/session binding
effective Native policy and complete eight-kind enforcement
typed SandboxPlan with Bubblewrap as pure actuator
real target permission and isolation qualification

d1_receipt.scope: pre-authority typed contract and current-policy shadow classification only
d1_receipt.canonical_argument_digest: sha256 over recursively key-sorted JSON arguments
tests: Native permission wire enums match the frozen eight-kind/two-scope/two-tool contract.
Permission request parsing rejects unknown tool/kind/scope, empty reason, non-object arguments and ttl outside 1..=3600.
Canonical argument digests are invariant under JSON object key order and change when bound arguments change.
Safe/trusted/dangerous implicit Native profiles are explicit typed data.

A shadow classifier reports only permission dimensions already enforced by the accepted Rust command policy and deliberately does not invent long_timeout, privileged_executable or write_generated_or_ignored semantics.

d2_receipt.scope: process-local explicit-grant ledger and unforgeable permit types; no production consent bridge or execution cutover
negative_tests: one-shot grant authorizes exactly one matching invocation
eight concurrent consumers of one once grant produce exactly one successful permit
session grant is reusable only inside the same process-local ledger
new authority instance cannot see an earlier session grant
grant debug output and stored records do not retain raw command arguments or expose the raw grant id

d3_contract.privileged_executable_rule: statically resolvable executable with setuid or setgid mode bits 0o6000
d3_contract.write_generated_or_ignored_rule: non-dry-run apply_patch touching a Git-ignored path or a canonical generated/excluded path component

d3_receipt.scope: shadow-only typed exec and patch invocation evaluation, runtime filesystem facts, deterministic effective policy, and atomic invocation-level grant lookup; no production permission or isolation cutover

command_risk_ordering: one safe-profile command combining sensitive environment, destructive command, shell expansion, inline script, network, 30001 ms timeout, and privileged executable reports all seven kinds in frozen order
boundary_values: timeouts 1 and 30000 do not require long_timeout
yield_time 30000 alone does not require long_timeout
command_parsing: cmd and argv parse to distinct typed forms
env assignment wrapper, pipeline, and && control segments expose every statically selected executable
quoted metacharacters and heredoc bodies do not become executable candidates
literal argv metacharacters do not become shell expansion
relative workspace executable and bare executable through the supplied sandbox PATH resolve without consulting login-shell PATH
unresolvable executable fails closed without exposing command text
setuid and setgid fixtures require privileged_executable
executable metadata mutation fails revalidation with NATIVE_EXECUTABLE_CHANGED
patch_classification: dry-run ignored add performs complete validation, requires no permission, and writes nothing
ignored update, ignored delete, move into ignored destination, and move out of ignored source all require write_generated_or_ignored
target is a canonical component while builder is not
root and nested Git ignore rules plus negation are honored
non-repository workspace succeeds and broken declared Git metadata fails closed
symlink destination is denied before authorization and remains unchanged
one-byte patch argument mutation cannot use or consume the original bound grant
multi_grant_atomicity: one of two required grants missing consumes neither
two once grants are consumed together exactly once
eight concurrent invocations over the same two once grants produce exactly one full winner
session plus once scope preserves reuse and one-shot semantics
expired plus valid and revoked plus valid sets consume no valid member
duplicate coverage fails closed and consumes none
cross-owner, cross-workspace, cross-tool, and argument-mutated bindings fail closed without partial consumption
secret_and_debug_behavior: typed invocation and patch-operation Debug omit raw command bodies, patch content, stdin, and environment values
Debug output for grant receipts and permits exposes no raw grant identifier
ledger records retain only canonical argument digests, not full argument JSON

d5a_contract.go_no_go_rule: Do not cut production permission authority over until a real MCP client declares form elicitation, presents an independent human approval UI, and the complete redacted D5A evidence passes.

acceptance.A0: Formatting, warnings-denied Clippy, workspace tests, governance, record-layout and unified local gate pass.
acceptance.A1: Typed permission wire values, normalization, classifier ordering and current safe/trusted/dangerous compatibility are frozen by golden/adversarial tests.
acceptance.A3: Grant binding, expiry, revocation, replay, concurrency, environment/path isolation and workflow-authority non-inheritance fail closed.
acceptance.A4: Real Bubblewrap target validation covers the complete permission surface plus network/DNS, TTY, timeout/kill, Sage, Magma, LaTeX and Git without new authority leakage.

non_goals: No new public tool or workflow capability.
No permission-grant persistence in workflow/project SQLite.
No silent consent inferred from request_permissions invocation.
rollback: Before permission-authority cutover, remove the MTM-014 shadow types/ledger and retain stable 0.4.0 Native policy plus Bubblewrap. After a later cutover, restore the frozen pre-cutover evaluator and invalidate all process-local grants; no persistent workflow/project/proof data rewrite is required.
manual_pending: D5A human MRTR form elicitation is accepted on MCP Inspector 2.5.0; production exec_command/apply_patch permission enforcement must remain pre-cutover until the complete real-target A4 corpus passes.
Real target A4 is required before any MTM-014 permission-authority cutover.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: Pending consent challenges had no table capacity or proactive-on-issuance expiry pruning, and grant records accumulated indefinitely. An authenticated client could leave unanswered requests and grow process-local state without a fixed bound.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Freeze global/per-owner and UTF-8 byte limits, prune expired records in the admission critical section, retain live and unexpired replay tombstones, reject capacity exhaustion without authority, and validate concurrent admission plus two real OAuth clients. No background worker or public exec/patch cutover was added.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.stage: candidate TTY lifecycle test command selection
recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first TTY test used sh -c with the shell builtin read; executable-fact collection treated that builtin as an unresolved statically inspectable executable and correctly failed closed before process start.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Kept the resolver fail-closed and changed only the test command to the already-supported sh -c printf form with tty=true. TTY transport then passed; stdin round-trip and descendant process-group behavior remain covered by the existing mtm-native lifecycle tests.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first Dangerous-mode candidate toolchain test incorrectly used a test-only runtime constructor whose exposure plan was hard-coded to DEFAULT_SANDBOX_PATH, causing Sage to fail closed as unresolved even though production NativeToolRuntime::new uses the real host PATH.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Aligned the test-only constructor with production PATH discovery without changing production code; Git, pdfLaTeX and Sage then passed through the candidate Bubblewrap path. Magma was separately identified as host-license blocked rather than an MTM resolution failure.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: Review found that two independently accepted challenges for the same owner/workspace/tool/permission/argument digest could both mint active grants. Authorization would then correctly fail as ambiguous, but a normal repeated user approval could therefore make an otherwise valid invocation unusable.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Made active exact grant issuance unique inside the grant-ledger mutex, added already_granted short-circuiting only for fresh first-round permission requests, preserved stale requestState replay denial, retained the ambiguous-ledger fail-closed path for legacy/corrupt state, and added lifecycle plus concurrent issuance tests. The MRTR corpus now passes 22 checks.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.stage: pre-cutover candidate dead-code tripwire under all-target test build
recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: After candidate tests began exercising the previously unreachable prepared-command symbols, warnings-denied Clippy correctly reported their unconditional expect(dead_code) annotations as unfulfilled in the test build.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Scoped the dead-code expectations to non-test builds with cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code)); production compilation still proves the candidate is unreachable while test compilation must exercise it without suppressing warnings.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Updated only the frozen governance assertion to mrtr_permission_bridge_integration, reran the unchanged runtime plus unified gate, and obtained all 24 repository checks passing.
